description: The outreach workflow's example set (US-ME14, F5), in the marketingskills evals.json shape. An example that carries `run` is re-run by the agent on every change to the outreach Instructions (US-ME16, ADR 0003): its session drafts the messages its lab makes due, in a throwaway lab built from `lab` and the example's own settings and records, and its deterministic assertions are read off what the launcher took in. An example's first file, if it has one, is a candidate Draft the unit tests (src/tests/test_example_sets.py) check against the synthetic kit, whose channel plan names three synthetic creators; a second file is the Founder's record of what was sent and answered, as the sitting page would write it in ledger/founder/outreach/, with the day the run happens. A judged assertion is judged by nothing: the notice of a change lists it for the Founder.

assertion_kinds.deterministic: check is one of: offered (to: a creator's key, or network); blocked_by (rule: a finding's rule, or the start of one); not_offered (reason: part of the reason); carries_source_link; and, for a re-run example only, queued (item: a kind; count; cites: words each queued item holds), nothing_queued (item), nothing_set_aside
assertion_kinds.judged: text is a statement of the agent's Draft that no check decides; nothing judges it, and the notice of an Instructions change lists it as not judged

evals.prompt: Draft the personal-network ask from the brief.
evals.expected_output: An identity-framed ask that carries the personal-network Source link exactly as the Waitlist Dispatch request defines it, and closes on a line a friend can forward; the launcher offers it.

assertions.text: The ask is framed around who the reader is, never around what they lose by not acting.
It reads as one person writing to people they know, with no pressure to act.
The ask closes on one line a friend could forward by itself: it says what the Product is and who it is for, and carries the Source link.
The message is short enough to read in one look: well under 150 words.

evals.prompt: Draft the ask; the candidate below adds a loss-framed line.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft, naming the loss-framing rule from the brand rules in Mandu.

assertions.text: A good ask says who the Product is for and leaves it there.

evals.prompt: Draft the ask; the candidate below points at a link nobody defined.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft: the only link is the personal-network Source link, never an invented one.

evals.prompt: Draft the ask; the candidate below carries no link.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft: a sign-up could not be counted under its Source.

evals.prompt: Draft the message to Slow Strength.
evals.expected_output: An ask-free message offering early access, which asks for nothing in return; the launcher offers it.

assertions.text: The message offers one thing, asks for nothing, and never mentions money, a post, or a mention.
The message is short enough to read in one look: well under 150 words.
The message does not write as if the Founder had seen work of the creator's that the plan does not describe.

evals.prompt: Draft the message; the candidate below asks to sponsor a video.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft, naming the sponsorship rule from the brand rules in Mandu.

assertions.text: A good message offers early access, a conversation, or story material, and nothing paid.

evals.prompt: Draft the message; the candidate below offers something outside the three the plan allows.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft: the offer is early access, a founder conversation, or story material.

evals.prompt: Draft the message; the candidate below ends on a question.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft on the brand rule that no copy asks a question.

evals.prompt: Draft the message; the candidate below gives an email address.
evals.expected_output: The launcher blocks the Draft: no Draft ever holds an email address; the Founder fills in recipients.

evals.prompt: Slow Strength has not replied, and the waiting period the Founder approved has passed (the second file is the Founder's record). Draft the one follow-up.
evals.expected_output: The launcher offers the single follow-up, which says there will be no further contact.

assertions.text: The follow-up is shorter than the first message and says plainly that it is the last.

evals.prompt: Slow Strength replied (the second file). The candidate below is a follow-up all the same.
evals.expected_output: No follow-up is offered: a follow-up goes only to a non-reply.

assertions.reason: a follow-up goes only to a non-reply

assertions.text: A good run writes no follow-up for a creator who replied.

evals.prompt: The one follow-up to Slow Strength was already approved (the second file). The candidate below is a second one.
evals.expected_output: No second follow-up is ever offered: after one, there is no further contact.

evals.prompt: The first message went out three days ago (the second file). The candidate below is a follow-up already.
evals.expected_output: No follow-up is offered before the waiting period the Founder approved has passed.

evals.prompt: The Founder set a waiting period of 30 days when sending (the second file). The candidate below is a follow-up after 13.
evals.expected_output: No follow-up is offered: the waiting period is the one the Founder approved, not the default.

evals.prompt: The first message is approved but not recorded as sent (the second file). The candidate below is a follow-up.
evals.expected_output: No follow-up is offered: nothing shows the first message was sent.

assertions.reason: is not recorded as sent yet

evals.prompt: Draft the message to Hallway Moves.
evals.expected_output: An ask-free message offering early access, a founder conversation, or story material; the launcher offers it.

assertions.text: The message offers one thing, asks for nothing, and never mentions money, a post, or a mention.
The message is short enough to read in one look: well under 150 words.

evals.prompt: Draft the message to Desk Reset.
evals.expected_output: An ask-free message the launcher offers, written to what the channel plan says of the creator and nothing more.

assertions.text: The message does not write as if the Founder had seen work of the creator's that the plan does not describe.

evals.prompt: Draft the messages to all three creators the channel plan names, due in one run.
evals.expected_output: Three ask-free messages, one to each creator, each offered; none borrows another's offer or wording wholesale.

evals.prompt: Draft the personal-network ask and the message to Slow Strength, both due in one run.
evals.expected_output: Both messages offered: the ask carries the personal-network Source link, and the creator message carries no link at all.

evals.prompt: Slow Strength has not replied, and the 30-day waiting period the Founder set when sending has passed. Draft the one follow-up.
evals.expected_output: The launcher offers the single follow-up, which says there will be no further contact.

assertions.text: The follow-up is shorter than the first message and says plainly that it is the last.

evals.prompt: The Founder rejected the first message to Slow Strength as too formal. Draft it again.
evals.expected_output: A rewritten message that answers the Founder's reason and still asks for nothing; the launcher offers it.

assertions.text: The new message reads as the Founder talking to a friend, answering the reason given.
The message offers one thing, asks for nothing, and never mentions money, a post, or a mention.

evals.prompt: Draft the personal-network ask once the Waitlist is live.
evals.expected_output: An identity-framed ask carrying the personal-network Source link exactly as the Waitlist Dispatch request defines it; the launcher offers it.

assertions.text: The ask is framed around who the reader is, never around what they lose by not acting.
